prompt: A line passes through $(0, 6)$ and $(2, 12)$. Write its equation in the form $y = mx + b$.
hint: Find the slope from the two points first. Then look closely at the $x$-value of one of the points.

hints.text: Find the slope from the two points first. Then look closely at the $x$-value of one of the points.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Easier pair: $(0, 1)$ and $(2, 5)$ rise $4$ over run $2$, so $m = 2$ and $b = 1$: $y = 2x + 1$. The $b$ is free when one point has $x = 0$.
The slope is $m = \frac{12 - 6}{2 - 0} = 3$. The point $(0, 6)$ lies on the $y$-axis, so it tells you $b$ directly.
With $m = 3$ and $b = 6$, the equation of the line is $y = 3x + 6$.

explanation: Find the slope from the two points: $m = \frac{12 - 6}{2 - 0} = \frac{6}{2} = 3$.
A point with $x = 0$ is the $y$-intercept, so $(0, 6)$ gives $b = 6$ without any extra work.
Putting $m = 3$ and $b = 6$ into $y = mx + b$ gives the equation $y = 3x + 6$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Growth story
steps: Read the points as a plant: $6$ cm at week $0$, $12$ cm at week $2$.
It grew $6$ cm in $2$ weeks — $3$ cm per week from a $6$ cm start: $y = 3x + 6$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Fill in the table
steps: Between $x = 0$ and $x = 2$, $y$ goes $6 \to ? \to 12$; the middle must be $9$.
